q-10091.name: Question 1
q-10091.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+2z=0 \\ x+2y+3z=2 \\ 3x+y+z=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
q-10091.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-1(1-9)+2(1-6) \\  & =+8-10 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 & -5 \\ -1 & -6 & -3 \\ -1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 8 & -5 \\ 1 & -6 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & 2 \\ -5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -1 \\ 8 & -6 & 2 \\ -5 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -2 \\ 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -2 \\ 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2} \\ 9 \\ -\frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-\frac{5}{2},y=9,z=-\frac{9}{2}.$

q-78559.name: Question 2
q-78559.problem:
Consider a system of $n$ linear equations in $n$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,z=c.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $z$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $c$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & =c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and right to left, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
q-78559.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,z=c$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & ={D}^{-1}c \\ {I}_{n}\,z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and ${I}_{n}.$

q-78559.html:
Question 2
?

Consider a system of n linear equations in n variables, written in matrix form as Dz=c. Here, D is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, z is the column vector containing the variables, and c is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

Dz=cD−1Dz=D−1cInz=D−1cz=D−1c

From top to bottom and right to left, what are the missing parts of the derivation?

a
D−1 and D
b
D−1 and D−1
c
D and z
d
D−1 and In
e
D and In
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since D is not singular, it must have an inverse D−1. Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation Dz=c by D−1, we obtain the following:

Dz=cD−1Dz=D−1cInz=D−1cz=D−1c

Therefore, the missing parts are D−1 and In.

q-78570.name: Question 3
q-78570.problem: Consider a matrix equation ${A}^{-1}\,x=B\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $7\times 7$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $7\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
q-78570.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${A}^{-1}\,x=B\,d$ by $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}\,x & =B\,d \\ A{A}^{-1}\,x & =AB\,d \\ {I}_{7}\,x & =AB\,d \\ x & =AB\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
